skill.description: Project-level guidance for LLM-powered systems, including task fit, staged pipeline design, cost estimation, structured outputs, and agent-assisted iteration.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, inline code, reference URLs, and CSS. The executable Python template does perform local file writes, and its path construction lacks validation for batch identifiers. No evidence of prompt injection or data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated batch and item path components
remediation.suggestion: Normalize paths with Path.resolve and reject absolute paths or parent-directory segments before writing or deleting files.

remediation.issue: Unescaped batch identifier in generated HTML
remediation.suggestion: Escape batch_id before inserting it into HTML title and heading fields.

remediation.issue: Script filesystem effects are not highlighted to users
remediation.suggestion: Document that the template writes and deletes local pipeline files, and recommend reviewing output directories before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Pipeline Paths Can Escape Output Directories
semantic_findings.description: The script builds data and output paths directly from batch_id and item_id values, then writes or deletes stage files under those paths. A parent-directory segment can move operations outside the intended data and output directories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path construction and CLI assignment are explicit, and clean uses unlink on derived paths. The impact depends on supplied batch IDs or customized item IDs.

semantic_findings.title: Generated HTML Uses Unescaped Batch Identifier
semantic_findings.description: The HTML renderer inserts batch_id into the page title and heading without escaping. A crafted batch identifier could inject markup into the generated local report.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The f-string inserts batch_id directly into HTML while other fields are escaped. The exposure is local generated output, so the severity is limited.

content.value_statement: LLM projects often fail when teams skip task fit, cost, and pipeline design. This skill guides staged architecture, structured outputs, and iteration plans.
actual_capabilities: Helps decide whether an LLM is suitable for a project task.
Defines staged acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render pipelines.
Explains file-system state and caching for batch workflows.
Provides cost estimation methods for token-heavy processing.
Compares single-agent and multi-agent project structures.
Includes a Python pipeline template for local prototyping.
limitations: Does not replace detailed tool interface design.
Does not provide production API integrations without customization.
Requires security review before running or modifying scripts.
Focuses on project-scale LLM workflows, not simple single prompts.

use_cases.title: Design a Batch Analysis Pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan stages, files, parsing, and rendering before building a large LLM batch workflow.

use_cases.title: Estimate an LLM Project
use_cases.description: Assess task fit, token cost, schedule, and operational risk before committing engineering time.

use_cases.title: Choose Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare single-agent and multi-agent designs using project constraints and measurable quality goals.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Task Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new LLM idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-development to assess whether this task fits an LLM. Cover task traits, risks, manual validation, and a proceed-or-stop recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Pipeline Stages
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a batch workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-development to design an acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render pipeline for this workflow. Include stage outputs and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Cost and Scale
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-development to estimate tokens, cost, retries, timeline, and bottlenecks for this LLM pipeline. Suggest ways to reduce cost safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing proposal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-development to review this architecture. Compare single-agent and multi-agent options, identify failure modes, and propose an iteration plan.

output_examples.input: A team wants to analyze 50,000 support tickets with an LLM.
output_examples.output: A staged pipeline plan with task-fit guidance, cache points, parsing requirements, cost estimates, and quality checks.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs to decide whether an agent system is worth building.
output_examples.output: A proceed-or-stop recommendation with model-fit criteria, expected costs, manual prototype steps, and delivery risks.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead has a multi-agent proposal for research workflows.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff review that compares simpler pipeline options, context limits, evaluation needs, and operational complexity.

best_practices: Validate task fit with a manual prototype before building automation.
Keep deterministic stages separate from LLM processing stages.
Estimate token cost early and track real usage during development.
anti_patterns: Do not build a monolithic pipeline that hides intermediate state.
Do not add multi-agent complexity before measuring single-agent limits.
Do not assume LLM output will follow format instructions perfectly.

faq.question: What kind of projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports LLM-heavy projects, batch workflows, agent applications, and multi-stage analysis pipelines.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and a prototype pipeline template that needs project-specific changes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: When should I avoid using this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for single prompt tasks, detailed tool schema design, or narrow context optimization work.

faq.question: Does it include cost planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains token estimation, scale planning, and cost buffers for retries and failures.

faq.question: Is the included script safe to run unchanged?
faq.answer: Review it first. It writes local files and should be customized with path validation and API integrations.
